signals.text: The wordcount output line reports words, characters and lines, but gives no byte size of the input.
For non-ASCII text the byte count differs from the character count: 'café' is 4 characters but 5 bytes in UTF-8.
signals.possible_indication: The character count cannot stand in for the byte count, so users have no correct size today.

signals.text: Users who size buffers, uploads or storage need the byte count of the input.
signals.possible_indication: The byte count may need to reflect the raw input bytes, not a re-encoded form of the decoded text.

signals.text: The user wants the byte count shown next to the characters count.
signals.possible_indication: The new field likely sits beside the existing counts on the same output line.

signals.text: The byte count must be available for input read from a file and from standard input through '-'.
signals.possible_indication: The same bytes should give the same byte count whether read from a file or from standard input.

DISCOVER.core_issue: wordcount users cannot learn the byte size of their input. The existing counts do not give it for non-ASCII text.
DISCOVER.impact_value: Users who size buffers, uploads or storage could get the byte size from wordcount. They would not need a second tool.
DISCOVER.discovery_method: Written feature intent and user notes from the handoff.
DISCOVER.pattern_dependencies: The byte-count-input-parity pattern depends on byte-count-missing. Parity only matters once a byte count exists. Both patterns build on the existing file and standard input paths from SPEC-0004.

pattern_narratives.applies_to: The wordcount output line for file and standard input
pattern_narratives.current_state: The output shows words, characters and lines. Users must use another tool to get the byte size.

pattern_narratives.frequency: Every run that reads standard input
pattern_narratives.current_state: File and standard input already give identical three-field output for the same bytes. No byte field exists on either path.
